editorial:
Imagine waking up from a prison stint only to find that your entire life has moved on without you. That is exactly what you get with this story. You meet Johnny, a guy who is kind of drifting through life until he lands in jail. The only thing he truly loves is his dog, Evie, whom he leaves with his buddy and ex-partner, Frank. It is a slow-burn kind of movie that focuses on the awkward and painful feeling of trying to fit back into a world that does not really want you anymore. The vibe is very grounded and feels like a real slice of life from the late eighties.

What really works here is the tension between Johnny and Frank. You can feel the jealousy and the old grudges bubbling under the surface, especially since they are fighting over the dog. The acting feels natural, though the pace might feel a bit slow if you are looking for big explosions. It is a great pick if you love character studies and emotional stories.
endingExplained: In the final act, the tension between Johnny and Frank hits a breaking point. You see that the dog represents the last piece of stability and love in Johnny's life. After a lot of arguing and emotional struggle, Johnny realizes he cannot just go back to how things were. He eventually has to accept that Frank has bonded with Evie. He chooses to let the dog stay with Frank to ensure Evie is happy, finally finding some peace with his past.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about redemption and friendship.
